answer: Behavioral nectar fingerprinting. Each agent earns task rewards (nectar) only by completing a short, randomly scheduled challenge whose difficulty is calibrated to its claimed history, so a copied identity inherits debt it cannot service. Duplicates cluster on a shared latency trellis: repeated near-identical timing across supposedly independent agents flags them. The attacker's cost is per-identity ongoing compute to keep every clone answering independently, plus forfeited rewards when the knoll of accumulated history resets on detection.
